nodes.title: kon/place measure: after 'Rakh do' she TYPES the reading on a number pad (0-9, delete; 0 … 180); no tap on the board prints a value and the band tap is gone (the game never reads the scale for her: dc-r8-game-modes-three-laws). The number decides the scale: within ±2 of the scale whose 0 is on the placed arm is right, within ±2 of 180 minus it is wrong-scale. Cost: after the lock the controls take three rows, so at 360 px the board scales to about 0.87 CSS px per board px (the protractor about 185 px wide) while she reads; before the lock it keeps two rows. Reverse if: children on a phone cannot read the 5° ticks at the locked size (then a magnified view of the scale, never a printed value).

kon: a mix-up made by one pick among few is a SIGN, not a named misconception (law 3): kon/name find's first-letter arc (one tap among five) and kon/place draw's right mark joined to A (one of two buttons) are law_refused moments with facts.sign = the mal-rule id and no misconceptionId, so nothing reaches her record from one pick; their rules no longer map the mix-up (find {}, draw {wrong-scale, vertex-off}). Naming them on a repeat on a level with a different surface, or when a constructed act agrees (a say miss), needs session memory the play server does not keep yet (server/play/levels.js afterLevelBody): proposed for main, not built. Reverse if: the sign is never read by anything (then drop it) or a session aggregator lands (then name on the repeat).

kon/place measure and draw: wrong-scale is discriminated (malActs non-null, so the level's proof lists it) only on levels where the outer scale is the wrong one at the placement the level is built for (the angle opens clockwise: mirror), and the rules list it first, so a first-try solve there carries discriminates = wrong-scale ('chose the right scale') and elsewhere it carries vertex-off only. The two orientations are served equally (mirror 0.45 → 0.5). The law still names wrong-scale wherever she types or marks 180 − θ (a constructed act). Reverse if: a child placing the base along OB (which flips which scale is right) turns out to be common.

kon/name find, after a wrong tap: her arc in the mix-up colour, and in place of the asked name a row 'asked ≠ her arc's two names', e.g. '∠OPQ ≠ ∠QOP = ∠POQ' (the asked chip in ink, ≠ and her chip in the mix-up colour). It contradicts 'the same letters are the same angle' (the same three letters in another order are another angle; the reverse order is the same one) without stating the middle-letter rule and without showing where the asked angle is. Reverse if: two judges or a pilot find children read it as a rule they cannot use, or it lets them home in on the key.

kon/name: the two arcs at the vertex between neighbouring rays are DRAWN at different radii (DRAW_R 42 and 58, a 16 px step where they meet on the shared ray) while the tap model keeps ARC_R 50/50: a model at different radii gave 0 of 283 figures a 48 px touch disc per arc (the outer arc's band is squeezed between BAND from the vertex and the wide arc), so drawing and tapping were decoupled; every point of each drawn arc taps its own arc (pinned). The joined pair is always two neighbouring ray ends (1-3 always crossed ray 2), O and Q are never in one figure, at fade 1 the vertex is O only in her first level of the mode (req.recent has no name signature), and say's dashed mix-up arc is ≥ 24 board px long (its angle ≥ 20°, radius ≤ 72). Reverse if: a tap on a drawn arc lands on its neighbour in a pilot.

kon/name picker CPU after the round-2 figure rules (tests/_cpu-ms.mjs cpuNow, pickLevels × 30 requests, say + find, fades 1-3, seeds 700-714, five repeats in one process, this container): p95 16.0-20.3 ms after the first (JIT) repeat, 29.4 ms on it; bar 50 ms; main's figure before the change about 24 ms. kon/place: p95 4.9-8.1 ms (18.9 on the first repeat).
